Build a Random-Forest Learner Adapter (Calibrated, Scoped)

make_ranger_adapter.Rd

Learner adapter extending STABL to non-linear signals with random forests (ranger). One forest is fit per bootstrap subsample; the "penalty path" is an importance-threshold path built from quantiles of the pooled permutation-importance distribution (see auto_rf_threshold_grid()), so the selection set grows monotonically as the threshold decreases — the same sparse-to-dense nesting the lambda path provides for glmnet learners.

Usage

make_ranger_adapter(num_trees = 500L)

Arguments

num_trees

Positive integer; number of trees per ranger forest.

Value

A function with signature function(x, y, lambda_val) -> logical vector of length ncol(x), mirroring make_glmnet_adapter(): the mask selects features whose permutation importance meets the threshold carried by lambda_val.

Details

Calibrated within a measured scope (WS-2, 60 simulation runs): with knockoff_equi decoys the mean empirical FDP is 0.025 on a linear design and 0.065 on a low-dimensional nonlinear design (p = 10), meeting the predeclared criterion (FDP <= 0.15, TPR >= 0.8). The criterion is NOT met on a high-dimensional correlated design at p = 50 (mean FDP 0.44) or for binary outcomes (0.26); avoid this pairing there. This is simulation evidence, not a guarantee for your dataset.

Statistical guardrails: permutation importance is used (not Gini). Random forests must be paired with model-X knockoff artificial features (knockoff_equi / knockoff_mvr): permuted nulls do not receive the correlation leakage that real null features receive in a multivariate learner, so random_permutation nulls make FDP+ anti-conservative — stablr warns when this combination is requested.

See also

auto_rf_threshold_grid(), make_glmnet_adapter(), stabl_fit() (base_learner = "rf").

Examples

if (requireNamespace("ranger", quietly = TRUE)) {
  set.seed(1L)
  x <- matrix(rnorm(60 * 6), 60, 6,
              dimnames = list(paste0("s", 1:60), paste0("f", 1:6)))
  y <- setNames(x[, 1] * x[, 2] * 0.5 + rnorm(60, sd = 0.3), rownames(x))
  adapter <- make_ranger_adapter(num_trees = 100L)
  grid <- auto_rf_threshold_grid(x, y, n_grid = 5L, num_trees = 100L, seed = 1L)
  mask <- adapter(x, y, grid[1L, ])  # sparsest end of the path
  cat("selected:", sum(mask), "of", ncol(x), "features\n")
}
#> selected: 0 of 6 features
